platformHome.title: Platform public home
platformHome.heroDescription: The platform homepage explains the system, the three-surface architecture, and the entry model. It is not a back-office entry page. Platform and tenant management spaces should only be reached after authorization, without exposing concrete admin addresses on the public page.
platformHome.fallbackDescription: A unified SaaS foundation for platform governance, tenant operations, and tenant-facing AI services.
platformHome.tenantAccessTitle: Tenant-side access belongs to tenant domains
platformHome.tenantAccessDescription: The tenant brand portal, tenant admin console, and tenant user homepage should not be mixed into the platform public homepage. Tenant-facing experiences should be reached through bound tenant domains.
platformHome.architectureDescription: The public homepage introduces the system, dashboard pages handle administration, and tenant domains host the branded front stage plus the post-login user home.
platformHome.nextStepsDescription: Separating the public homepage, dashboard homepages, and tenant-facing entries makes the product story much easier to demonstrate.

tenancy.title: Multi-tenancy and branding
tenancy.description: Split platform domains from tenant domains so every tenant can own a branded portal, admin console, and user-facing front stage.

ai.title: AI service chain
ai.description: Reuse the existing agents, knowledge bases, conversations, attachments, and page capabilities to present AI as a real product feature.

security.title: Permissions and isolation
security.description: Platform admins, tenant admins, and tenant users keep clean boundaries across permissions, menus, and session contexts.

extension.title: Extensible foundation
extension.description: Plugins, configurations, jobs, logs, and AI modules remain extensible for both demo use and real deployment.

platform.title: Platform public home + platform console
platform.description: The platform public homepage is only for product introduction. Management workspaces stay strictly separated from the public surface.

tenant.title: Tenant brand portal + tenant admin console
tenant.description: A tenant domain serves branded public access and post-login business experiences, while management space should not be exposed directly on the public page.

user.title: Tenant user homepage + AI pages
user.description: After sign-in, tenant users still land on /, but that same path now becomes the post-login workspace that leads into /agents, /ai-chat, and /help.

highlights.branding: The platform homepage no longer misroutes visitors straight into the admin area.
highlights.rbac: The tenant root path can switch between a public brand portal and a post-login workspace.
highlights.rag: All AI execution pages are moved behind authentication.
highlights.workflow: Dashboard pages keep their original role and only receive visual and hierarchy improvements.

nextSteps.platformTitle: Separate platform introduction from platform management
nextSteps.platformDescription: Visitors should understand the product from the public homepage first, then authorized operators enter management through controlled flows.
nextSteps.tenantTitle: Separate tenant branding from tenant administration
nextSteps.tenantDescription: Tenant visitors see the brand portal first, while signed-in users and operators continue into their own protected spaces.
nextSteps.userTitle: Link the tenant user homepage to AI features
nextSteps.userDescription: After sign-in, tenant users arrive at / and continue into the agent plaza, AI chat, and help center from that homepage.
